# The brain and nerves (seat of thought, electrical signalling) (`nervous_system_brain`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/biology.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Life sciences (`biology`)
- Deps: helped by anatomy_dissection, electric_battery, microscope, natural_causes
- Core idea: Thought, feeling, sensation and the command of movement sit in the brain, not in the heart, and reach the body through the nerves, which are cords of signalling fibres, not hollow tubes carrying a spirit. Damage to a motor nerve weakens the muscles it supplies; sensory nerve damage can cause numbness. A stroke on one side of the brain can impair movement on the opposite side. The pattern of loss helps locate the injury. The signal is electrical: a frog's leg twitches when its nerve is touched with two different metals joined together, or with the wires of a battery. It travels at speeds ranging from under one metre a second in thin, unmyelinated fibres to over 100 in large, myelinated ones. Different parts of the brain do different work.
- Pitfalls:
  - The Aristotelian view that the heart thinks and the brain cools the blood
  - Placing the mind in the fluid-filled cavities of the brain, a widespread medieval teaching
  - Phrenology: reading character from bumps on the skull
  - Modern myths such as 'we use only 10 % of the brain' or strict left-brain and right-brain personalities
  - Supposing nerves conduct like copper wires
- History: egypt: c. 1600 BC – Edwin Smith papyrus links head wounds to paralysis and loss of speech; c. 300 BC Herophilus in Alexandria separates nerves from tendons and traces them to the brain; greece: c. 450 BC – Alcmaeon of Croton places sensation in the brain; c. 400 BC the Hippocratic 'On the Sacred Disease' calls epilepsy a natural brain disease; 4th c. BC Aristotle prefers the heart; rome: 2nd c. AD – Galen silences a squealing pig by tying the nerves to its voice box; islamic: 11th c. – Ibn Sina and others assign faculties to the brain's cavities; europe: 1664 – Willis, anatomy of the brain; 1791 Galvani's animal electricity; 1811–1822 Bell and Magendie separate sensory and motor nerve roots; 1850 Helmholtz measures the speed of the nerve signal; 1861 Broca locates a speech area; 1888 Ramón y Cajal shows nerve cells are separate units; 1929 Berger's recordings of brain waves
- Read:
  - Luigi Galvani, De viribus electricitatis in motu musculari commentarius (1791)
  - Stanley Finger, Origins of Neuroscience: A History of Explorations into Brain Function (1994)
  - Matthew Cobb, The Idea of the Brain (2020)
  - Dale Purves et al. (eds.), Neuroscience (2nd ed., 2001), Increased Conduction Velocity as a Result of Myelination
